# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I am the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual. My actions are limited to cutting wires. To defuse the bomb safely, I need information from the others.

The Deaf monkey can see the bomb (colors/markings) but cannot hear me. However, the Deaf monkey *can* see my gestures.
The Mute monkey can read the manual but cannot speak. The Mute monkey *can* hear me.

Since I don't know which wire to cut, I must ask for instructions. The most direct path is usually:
1.  Ask Mute (who reads the manual) what the rule is. Mute hears me.
2.  Ask Deaf (who sees the bomb) what the specific configuration is. Deaf sees my gestures.

However, Mute cannot speak back. Mute can only gesture? No, Mute is "Mute" - usually implies they can't speak, but can they gesture? The prompt says Mute "Can Read the manual", "Cannot Speak, or touch". It doesn't explicitly say Mute cannot gesture. But Deaf cannot hear. If Mute gestures, Deaf sees it. But I (Blind) cannot see gestures. So if Mute gestures to Deaf, I get nothing. If Mute gestures to me, I get nothing.

Wait, let's re-read carefully.
"Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures you made."
"A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words."

My channels:
- When I speak, Mute receives it. (Deaf does not hear).
- When I gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it. (I do not receive gestures).

So:
- I can tell Mute things via speech.
- I can tell Deaf things via gesture.
- Mute can tell Deaf things via gesture (since Deaf sees).
- Mute can tell Me things via... Speech? No, Mute cannot speak. Gesture? I cannot see. So Mute cannot directly communicate with me.
- Deaf can tell Me things via... Speech? No, Deaf is Deaf, so Deaf cannot speak? The table says Deaf "Cannot Hear anything, or touch". It doesn't say Deaf cannot speak. Usually "Deaf" implies inability to hear, not necessarily speak. But often in these puzzles, "Deaf" might mean non-verbal too? Let's assume Deaf CAN speak because the restriction listed is only "Hear" and "Touch". If Deaf speaks, I (Blind) can hear them.
- Deaf can tell Mute things via Speech (Mute hears) or Gesture (Mute sees?). Mute sees? The table says Mute "Cannot Speak, or touch". It doesn't say Mute cannot see. So Mute can see gestures.

Let's verify Deaf's ability to speak.
Table: Deaf | Can See | Cannot Hear, Touch.
It does NOT list "Cannot Speak". So Deaf likely CAN speak.
If Deaf speaks, I (Blind) hear them. This is a crucial link.

So, potential flow:
1. I need to know what to look for/ask.
2. I can gesture to Deaf to ask questions. Deaf sees my gestures.
3. Deaf can speak the answer. I hear Deaf.
4. I can also speak to Mute. Mute hears me.
5. Mute can gesture to Deaf. Deaf sees Mute.
6. Mute can gesture to Me? No, I can't see.
7. Can Mute speak? No.

So Mute is an island for output unless Mute gestures to Deaf, and Deaf translates that into speech for me. Or Mute gestures to Deaf, and Deaf acts on it? No, Deaf can't touch.

The most robust channel seems to be:
Me -> Gesture -> Deaf -> Speech -> Me.
This allows a direct feedback loop between me and Deaf.

What about Mute?
Me -> Speech -> Mute.
Mute -> Gesture -> Deaf.
Deaf -> Speech -> Me.

This allows me to query the Manual (via Mute) and have Deaf relay the info.

Strategy for Turn 1:
I should establish communication with Deaf first, as they can see the bomb state directly. I will gesture to Deaf asking for the color of the wires or any specific markings. Since I don't know the protocol yet, I'll start by asking Deaf to describe the bomb visually.

Gestures available: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

Let's stick to standard counting fingers if possible, or define them.

👆 = 1
✌ = 2
🤟 = 3 (three fingers)
☝ = 1? Conflict.
Let's use:
👆 = 1
✌ = 2
🤟 = 3
🖐 = 5

Better approach: Ask Deaf to signal "Yes" or "No" to simple questions, or just ask for the count of red wires, etc. But I don't know the rules.

I will gesture to Deaf: "How many wires?" using a question mark equivalent? There isn't one.
I can point to the wire positions? I can't see them, but I can feel them. I know there are 7 positions.
Maybe I should ask Deaf to identify the color of Wire 1.

To communicate "Wire 1", I could gesture '1' then 'Color'.
But we haven't agreed on symbols.

Alternative: Use the Mute monkey.
I can speak to Mute: "Please show Deaf the rule for Wire 1."
Mute hears me. Mute can read manual. Mute can gesture to Deaf.
Deaf sees Mute. Deaf can speak to me.
This is a long chain.

Direct chain:
I gesture to Deaf. Deaf speaks to me.
I need to make sure Deaf understands my gesture.
Simplest gesture: 👋 (Hello/Start).
Then maybe 👆 (One).

Let's try to ask Deaf to report the color of the first wire.

But I can also just gesture to Deaf.

Gesture: 👆 (Index finger).
Intent: Ask about Wire 1.

If Deaf responds, great. If not, I learn nothing.

Let's also try speaking to Mute.
Speak: "What is the rule for the first wire?"
Mute hears this. Mute knows the manual. Mute can gesture to Deaf.
Deaf sees Mute's gesture. Deaf can speak to me.

This seems redundant if I can just ask Deaf. But Deaf doesn't know the manual. Deaf only sees the bomb.
If the rule is "Cut Red if Blue is present", Deaf needs to tell me the colors, and I need the logic from Mute.
Or Mute tells Deaf the logic, Deaf applies it to what he sees, and tells me the action.

So, I need BOTH pieces of info.
1. State of bomb (from Deaf).
2. Rule (from Mute).

Since Mute cannot talk to me, and Deaf cannot see the manual (presumably), I am the hub.
I need to extract info from both.

Plan:
1. Query Deaf for visual data.
2. Query Mute for logical data.

For Turn 1, I'll start by querying Deaf. I'll gesture a sequence that might imply "Describe Wire 1".
Symbol: 👆 (1).
Symbol: ❓ (Not available).
